solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bribe from worker collected by sponsor

indicators.note: to be collected by something is to be gathered up inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a backer is someone who sponsors or supports a venture
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A worker's bribe ends up in the hands of the person sponsoring them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'collected by' make it sound like money changing hands; the worker is simply placed inside the sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is informal British slang for a bribe, a payment slipped quietly to someone.

clue.text: Roll moulded with age rather fast

indicators.note: something moulded is reshaped, so these letters are pressed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bread roll shaped and left to age goes stale rather quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical tempo marking meaning brisk, quicker than moderato but short of presto.

clue.text: Kingdoms originally run with single currency

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Kingdoms
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
single means one

explanation.surface: Scandinavian kingdoms once operated under a shared single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits nicely: Denmark and Norway are kingdoms using the krone.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the monetary unit of Denmark and Norway, so it is a national currency.

clue.text: Unforeseen event upset inspector beset by stress

indicators.note: to be beset by something is to be surrounded on all sides by it

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks

explanation.surface: Something unexpected has unsettled a police inspector already under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is a mishap nobody planned or saw coming.

clue.text: Snapped kind of desultory rebuttal to delusional person

indicators.note: something snapped is broken apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: all fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone retorted sharply with an offhand put-down to a person living in a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped' reads as spoke curtly, setting up a terse reply, but it signals breaking the next three words apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock retort telling someone they are fooling themselves, so it rebuts a deluded person.

clue.text: Tell end of rib-tickler with delight

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the final letter of the hyphenated word

parts.note: the final letter of rib-tickler
to delight someone is to elate them

explanation.surface: Deliver the punchline of a good joke with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: Clean article covered in web

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is wrapped inside it

parts.note: a net is a mesh or web
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tidy piece of writing gets posted on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'web' suggests the internet, but it simply means a mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and clean both describe something tidy and orderly.

clue.text: Minor condition no issue, getting balder regularly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: getting here means receiving something into itself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: issue in the sense of offspring, as is seed

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept starting from the first

parts.note: letters one, three and five of balder

explanation.surface: A man going bald insists his trivial ailment is nothing to worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' here means offspring, an old sense the surface hides behind 'no problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebleed is a common, usually harmless ailment, so it counts as a minor medical complaint.

clue.text: Commercial on screen is source of guidance

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, AD for short
a visor is a screen shielding the eyes

explanation.surface: An advert on television is where people get their advice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece 'on' another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisor is a person who counsels others, so they are someone people turn to for guidance.

clue.text: Too casual, some coats

indicators.note: the preceding words coat the answer, wrapping around it so it lies concealed inside them

parts.note: runs across the end of casual and the start of some

explanation.surface: Wearing a few coats seems overly informal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' looks like the pointer to part of a word, but it is fodder; the clue says the two words before 'coats' cover the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and also are both adverbs meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Definite replacement of vice-consul

indicators.note: a replacement swaps things around, so these letters are put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: It is certain that a diplomat's deputy is being replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusive evidence settles a matter beyond doubt, so it is decisive or definite.

clue.text: Silver, hoofed animals returned and settled

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: deer are hoofed animals

explanation.surface: Silver was handed back and some herd animals came home, so the matter was resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed, as in an agreed price, means settled or decided by both sides.

clue.text: King dined with ex-President and singer

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
dined means ate
either George Bush, both former US presidents

explanation.surface: A monarch had dinner with a former American president and a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a state banquet guest list.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Bush is the English singer-songwriter famous for Wuthering Heights.

clue.text: Fraud punished and locked up

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fraud
being fined is a monetary punishment

explanation.surface: A fraudster was penalised and jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confined is to be shut in or imprisoned, which is what locked up means.

clue.text: Practical vehicle that's blue loudly crossing capital from south

indicators.note: crossing means spanning something, so the outer letters straddle the city's name
in a down clue, reading from the south means starting at the bottom and going up

parts.note: blue in the sense of risqué or slightly indecent
Lima is the capital of Peru
f is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A sensible car painted blue roars noisily through the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like the vehicle's colour, but it means risqué. RACY and F straddle LIMA, and the whole string is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A family car is a roomy, sensible model chosen for everyday usefulness rather than style.

clue.text: Aristocrat taking lead role in prime locations

indicators.note: prime locations are the positions numbered by prime numbers, two, three, five and seven

parts.note: letters two, three, five and seven of the two words

explanation.surface: A nobleman stars in productions staged at top venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime locations' sounds like choice property, but it means the prime-numbered positions in the phrase just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount, so he is a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Figure hugged by fellow author of spy novels

indicators.note: something hugged by another is held within its embrace

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college
eight is a figure, a numeral

explanation.surface: A writer of espionage thrillers is pictured being embraced by a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Len Deighton wrote The IPCRESS File and other Cold War spy thrillers.

clue.text: Secure gun after taking ear off

indicators.note: taking something off means removing it, so those letters are struck out

parts.note: a firearm is a gun
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Hold the weapon steady once the ear protection has come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' finishes the deletion phrase: taking EAR off FIREARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and secure both mean fixed steadily in place.

clue.text: Bill is popular tenor, perhaps

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a tenor is one type of singing voice

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is a famous tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is an account to be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent to request payment for goods or services.

clue.text: Cook too much; essentially conserve excess

parts.note: to overdo food is to overcook it

indicators.note: essentially points to a word's core, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of conserve

explanation.surface: Don't overboil the jam; there's surplus preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook too much' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay and the definition is the last word. Conserve here is jam.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdose is an excessive amount of something, especially of a drug.

clue.text: Tank is fine one scrubbed by fellow after aquatic creatures

indicators.note: scrubbed means cancelled or rubbed out, so these letters are removed from the other word

parts.note: a man who goes after fish is a fisherman
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fish tank is perfectly fine, cleaned out by an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: F and I are struck from the front of FISHERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherman was the main American tank of the Second World War.

clue.text: My knight and queen put in difficulty

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
N is the chess notation for knight
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: In chess, someone's knight and queen have been trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive but the exclamation, as in 'my, how surprising!'
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to trap them so they have no way out, leaving them in a tight spot.

clue.text: Nothing gained in bothering reviled miscreant

indicators.note: something gained in another is taken into it, so one piece is added inside
bothering suggests being stirred up and disturbed, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer who has been bothering people gets nothing from being despised.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, someone who behaves badly or breaks the law.

clue.text: Cut good timber case of elmwood

parts.note: G is the common abbreviation for good
ash is a hardwood timber

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of elmwood

explanation.surface: A woodworker slices quality timber for a box made of elm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashed means cut deeply, as with a long wound.

clue.text: Cook's small crew

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a crew is a team working together

explanation.surface: A chef has only a small kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook's' reads as possessive but is 'Cook is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam food is one way of cooking it, over boiling water.

clue.text: Fluster when two music events overlap

parts.note: tells us the next phrase supplies two separate words; it adds no letters

indicators.note: when two things overlap they share a stretch, so that shared stretch is written only once

parts.note: a disco is a dance event with music
a concert is a live music performance

explanation.surface: It is unsettling when two gigs are booked for the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' tells us the phrase supplies two separate words. The CO ending one begins the other, so it is written once.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert someone is to unsettle or fluster them.

clue.text: Woman fed mamba regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: letters two, four, six and eight of the two words

explanation.surface: A woman gives a snake its meals on a regular schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a woman's first name, standing in for any woman.

clue.text: Fruit couple picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Two people gather fruit from the orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' fits the fruit picking scene, but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet orchard fruit.

clue.text: Polish official joining eminent rogue

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a sports official

indicators.note: rogue means wayward or out of control, so these letters stray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Polish official teams up with a distinguished but dishonest person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the noun meaning sophistication.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish and refinement both mean elegance and cultivation of manner.
